description: Advance a temporary anonymous demo simulation by one time step, or batch 1–500 sequential steps in one MCP call. Anonymous demos remain capped at 20 persisted steps total; API-key clients can use the full 1–500 batch. MySQL databases automatically receive an additive metrics.mysqlPreparedStatementForecasts result (top-level mysqlPreparedStatementForecasts in compact and stateless results), without opt-in. Set characteristics.databaseEngineIdentity='mysql' or an authoritative MySQL identity; names do not qualify. Supplemental characteristics.mysqlPreparedStatementForecast supplies server caps, initial prepared/open counts, finite horizon, explicit timeOrigin, provenance and future offered-workload windows with open-connection profiles. Missing required inputs yield unavailable with missingInputs; no universal baseline/cap or pool-budget substitution. Crossings use seconds from the supplied origin, a 15-second grid and half-open windows; gaps advance time without offered volume. rungRps is null without explicit rungs; no_crossing_within_horizon is finite, not never. This forecast never injects errno 1461 or changes metrics/decisions. Conditional rung validation only: 2× m5.large + db.r5.large MySQL 8.0, max_connections 500, cap 24,630, cwm-bench f0e1c228; observed onset was 286–383 seconds earlier than forecast (late forecasts), not a timing pass. Other configurations are extrapolations. Source/parameters are not downloadable. A batch response contains the final step, not every intermediate row, even with responseMode:'full'. For a timeline, batch up to 500 steps within runtime budgets (and remaining demo quota), then read history once. The next tool is simulation.metrics with responseMode:'full'. Anonymous batching loops over separate UI step requests, reserving quota per executed sub-step, not per MCP call; it can stop at the 20-step cap and report batchStatus:'limit_reached' with batchStepsCompleted. Runtime budgets still apply. No API key required; only this session's owned demo simulations are accessible. Concurrent simulation.step calls on one simulation either serialize as distinct consecutive steps (in the browser Workspace queue) or receive HTTP 409 simulation_step_in_progress without advancing or consuming a demo credit. Wait for the running call to finish, then retry only rejected calls; distinct simulations can run concurrently. After a timeout, inspect simulation.metrics before retrying an uncertain result. Use it to observe how the architecture behaves over time, typically right after simulation.create or simulation.inject_traffic. Do not use it to read current state without advancing time — that is simulation.metrics. Pass the simulationId returned by simulation.create when your connector opens a fresh MCP session; preserve Mcp-Session-Id to use the omitted-ID current-simulation default. An optional traffic override is applied when no traffic pattern is active; with an active pattern it is rejected with STEP_TRAFFIC_PATTERN_ACTIVE. Use simulation.inject_traffic to change load; it deactivates patterns before replay finalization and uses a runtime-only override for finalized SQS backlog runs, or omit traffic to follow the schedule. The likely next tool is simulation.step again (to keep observing) or simulation.inject_traffic (to change load first). Responses are compact by default: principal metrics plus per-resource status (id, name, status, cpuPercent, routedRps, availabilityState, isRoutable, and recoveryBlockedReason when provided) and this step's events. Seeded characteristics.eksSpotInterruption telemetry retains its additive migrationEvaluation beside the interruption lifecycle: use its recorded/derived/unavailable field provenance, frozen deadline verdict/counts/reasons, and simulation-clock milestones rather than final service health. The distinct eksSpotMigration contract remains separately reported when configured. Compact responses also include errorBreakdown when the engine provides it. A critical resource with isRoutable: true is degraded but still serving; unavailable identifies a failed or parked node, while scaled_to_zero and cold_start identify Fargate no-task states. Pass responseMode: 'full' to get the complete simulation state instead. During recovery, each resource may include recoveryProgress with state parked, cooling_down, or healthy, plus parkWindow and cooldown counters. Poll simulation.step until the targeted resource's recoveryProgress.state is healthy, then use simulation.metrics to inspect the resulting state and metrics. GPU / inference workflow: when the simulation includes a kubernetes resource with characteristics.inferenceMode: true, each step response also includes gpuUtilization (%), tokensPerSecond, costPerMillionTokens (USD/M tokens), idleGpuCostPerHour (USD/hr of standby GPU spend), and idleGpuFraction (0-1 idle HA overhead share) so you can track inference economics step by step. Authenticate with an API key for unlimited steps and GPU right-sizing hints.

responseMode.description: Response detail level. 'compact' (default) returns only principal metrics, errorBreakdown when available, per-resource status (id, name, status, cpuPercent, routedRps, availabilityState, isRoutable, recoveryBlockedReason, and failureLifecycle/routingState when provided), and this step's events — keeps observations small for agent loops. 'full' returns the complete backend step response including the entire simulation object with all resource characteristics and connections.

simulationId.description: Simulation ID returned by simulation.create. Preserve Mcp-Session-Id to omit this field and use the session's current simulation; if your connector starts a fresh MCP session for each call (for example Grok Bot or Cursor), pass this explicit ID after every fresh initialization. A fresh session has no current-simulation pointer and returns NO_ACTIVE_SIMULATION when the ID is omitted. Anonymous capabilities are short-lived (30 minutes by default), unguessable, and revoked when the demo expires or is deleted; proxy IP changes do not invalidate them. Do not treat the ID as a durable share link.

steps.description: Run one deadline-bounded backend batch, subject to 20 demo steps. Only committed sub-steps consume quota. Supply operationId for replay after an uncertain response. A partial operation is terminal; continue with a new ID, remaining count and expectedCheckpoint. Next call simulation.metrics with responseMode:'full' for the timeline.

traffic.description: Optional RPS override for this step. Applied when no traffic pattern is active; otherwise rejected with STEP_TRAFFIC_PATTERN_ACTIVE. Use simulation.inject_traffic to change load; finalized SQS backlog runs keep the pattern snapshot and apply an explicit target at runtime.

name: simulation.step

outputSchema.description: Compact step summary by default (principal metrics + per-resource status), the complete backend step response with responseMode 'full', or a structured limit response (status: limit_reached) when the step cap is reached

auroraFailovers.description: Compact per-writer database failover state; promoting has no serving writer, serving means the explicitly related standby took over.

promotedResourceId.description: Promoted database resource ID; standbyResourceId is retained as a compatibility alias.

batchStatus.description: Present when an anonymous batch stopped at its remaining demo step limit.

batchStepsCompleted.description: Number of sequential steps completed in this MCP call.

batchStepsRequested.description: Number of sequential steps requested in one MCP call.

benchmarkCalibration.description: Per-step calibration provenance: MEASURED outputs at observed points, MODELED projection outside them, ASSUMED configuration, and the CWM model assumptions used.

calibrationId.description: Versioned owned calibration identifier; present only when that calibration applies.

kind.description: owned for the exact AWS CRUD fit; owned-scaled when derived from that fit outside its exact fleet size; modeled when the gate fails or another generic model applies.

latencyBasis.description: General modeled latency path, such as in-VPC ALB rather than end-to-end; see latencyP99Basis for percentile-specific P99 provenance.

latencyP99Basis.description: Percentile-specific P99 basis: owned in-VPC internal-ALB fit, scaled from that fit (not directly measured), or uncalibrated generic model.

note.description: Names the fit scope and limitations. For canonical workload inference, states it is a modeling assumption. For modeled fallback, names all actual failed checks in stable order with resource IDs and safe expected/actual values; never only a generic 'not applied'.

identity.description: Canonical Cloud SQL billing identity belongs only in characteristics.cloudSql. Example: {"characteristics":{"cloudSql":{"engine":"mysql","tier":"db-custom-2-7680","region":"us-central1","edition":"ENTERPRISE","availability":"ZONAL","diskType":"PD_SSD","allocatedGiB":100}}}. Misplaced edition, availability, diskType, allocatedGiB, databaseVersion, tier and HA/disk-specific inputs are rejected with field-specific errors. Shared characteristics.engine, size/instanceType, capacityGB and resource.location are supported aliases; conflicting nested/alias values are rejected. Missing fields remain explicit inputGaps; complete configurations without verified meters remain pricing evidence gaps, not missing inputs.

costComplete.description: Whether the estimated cost includes all resources.

costPerHour.description: Complete estimated cost in USD/hr; omitted from compact output when costComplete=false.

costPerMillionTokens.description: Self-hosted inference cost in USD per million tokens (null when no tokens are being processed) — present only on GPU inference simulations

costStatus.description: Whether the cost headline is complete. Incomplete output uses pricedResourceSubtotalPerHour instead of costPerHour.

declaredFleetConnectionBudgetBasis.const: ASSUMPTION / maximum declared fleet × app pool size; not observed live DB connections

loadDerivedBasis.const: load-derived estimate; not observed live DB connections

effectiveConfigHash.description: Versioned prediction hash over replay startup inputs, engine version, and calibration identity; see replayIdentity.effectiveConfigHash for the original replay-only hash.

eksSpotInterruptions.description: Seeded EKS interruption telemetry, including the authoritative additive migrationEvaluation when recorded.

checkpointEvidence.description: Persisted seeded-EKS checkpoint captured with its interruption JSONB record. engineInputStepIndex is an engine input-step index, simulationSeconds is derived from that index and the recorded tick, and traffic provenance points to outer metric fields rather than duplicating float values.

migrationEvaluation.description: Authoritative additive seeded EKS interruption evaluation. Field values carry recorded/derived/unavailable provenance; deadline verdict/counts/reasons are frozen once status is completed and do not describe later service health.

engineVersion.description: Simulation engine version used for this prediction.

errorBreakdown.description: Validated additive error contributors in percentage-point units; separates database connection pressure below the usable pool limit from pool saturation after exhaustion, plus DB, compute, capacity, CPU, storage, runtime-memory, and queue absorption effects

errorRate.description: Client-level error rate (%) against original offered RPS. Resilience dependency targets in autoscaled compute fleets use aggregate routable-fleet capacity and health; non-autoscaled targets use their resolved resource capacity, including any declared fixed-instance count.

events.description: Events generated during this step; every event has a non-empty canonical type

excludedCostDetails.description: Named resources excluded from the partial cost when costComplete=false.

excludedCostResources.description: Number of GPU resources omitted from costPerHour because their worker price could not be resolved.

externalMetrics.description: Latest deterministic external-metric recommendation telemetry, including each trigger's sample status/outcome/value/desired capacity and the combined capacity decision. It never actuates simulated or provider resources.

goodputProvenance.description: Provenance for the modeled goodput field

goodputRps.description: Modeled client-level successful requests per second; a post-step point rate sourced from metrics.throughput. Resilience dependency targets in autoscaled compute fleets use aggregate routable-fleet capacity and health; non-autoscaled targets use their resolved resource capacity, including any declared fixed-instance count.

goodputSemantics.description: Goodput is a point rate, not an interval total

goodputWindow.description: Interval goodput aggregate when every point has persisted simulation-clock bounds; otherwise status=unavailable. Never derive this from retrieval time or currentStep.

gpuReadinessLatencyBasis.description: When GPU readiness is configured, aggregate P95 is ESTIMATED from a generic non-GPU-specific reference.

gpuUtilization.description: GPU utilization (%) — present only on simulations with a GPU inference kubernetes resource

hint.description: Present on deadline partials: guidance for submitting the remaining ordinary owned steps as an authenticated step job.

idleGpuCostPerHour.description: USD/hr of GPU spend funding idle/standby capacity (HA overhead) — present only on GPU inference simulations

idleGpuFraction.description: Share (0-1) of the GPU bill that is idle/standby capacity — present only on GPU inference simulations; values above 0.5 mean over half the GPU spend is HA overhead

kubernetesCpuHpa.description: Per-workload CPU request, observed millicores per pod, target calculations, bounded replica recommendation, scale-down stabilization, and provenance/errors. Utilization without a CPU request has no recommendation; this is not Kubernetes controller parity.

modelScope.const: workload-replicas-only; no Kubernetes controller parity claim

latencyBasis.description: General modeled latency path/boundary; see latencyP99Basis for P99-specific provenance.

latencyP50.description: 50th-percentile latency in ms; null when workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable.

latencyP95.description: 95th-percentile latency in ms; null when workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable.

latencyP99.description: Modeled 99th-percentile latency in ms; null when workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable. Interpret with latencyP99Basis and predictionEvidence.latencyP99.

latencyP99Basis.description: Percentile-specific P99 basis: owned fit, scaled-from-fit (not directly measured), or uncalibrated generic model.

loadBalancers.description: Per-load-balancer routed traffic, including CDN-origin-matched ALB RPS for comparison with cdnFlow.originRps

routedRps.description: Requests per second routed through this load balancer this step

metricId.description: Storage-assigned persisted metric ID when available

metrics.description: Full-mode backend metric record; migrationEvaluation is exact-typed when a seeded interruption is present.

errorBreakdown.description: Full-mode error contributors, including cause-attributed pool-saturation details.

databasePressureDetails.description: Per-database causes contributing to pressure below the usable connection limit.

cause.description: Modeled source of this database's under-limit pressure contribution.

resourceId.description: Database resource ID contributing to modeled under-limit connection pressure.

poolSaturationDetails.description: Per-database pool exhaustion details, including the cause when available. Modeled demand is not observed live sessions.

cause.description: Why this database's modeled connection demand exceeded its usable pool limit.

demandBasis.const: modeled connection demand; not observed live sessions

modeledConnections.description: Modeled demand/assumption, not observed live sessions.

resourceId.description: Database resource ID whose modeled demand exceeds its usable limit.

usableConnectionLimit.description: This database's effective usable connection limit.

staleDNS.description: Modeled failed-request contribution in percentage points from stale DNS routing to unavailable regional compute; not an additional independent error rate.

gpuReadinessLatencyBasis.description: When GPU readiness is configured, aggregate P95 is ESTIMATED from a generic non-GPU-specific reference.

latencyBasis.description: General modeled latency path/boundary; see latencyP99Basis for P99-specific provenance.

latencyP50.description: 50th-percentile latency in ms; null when workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable.

latencyP95.description: 95th-percentile latency in ms; null when workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable.

latencyP99.description: Modeled 99th-percentile latency in ms; null when workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable. Interpret with this metric's latencyP99Basis and predictionEvidence.latencyP99.

latencyP99Basis.description: Percentile-specific P99 basis for this metric checkpoint.

modeledShedRps.description: Aggregate modeled requests per second shed by bounded capacity

normalizedConfig.description: Resolved billing, exclusions and capacity, consistent with create/get; performance may be estimated even when prices are verified.

resources.description: Per-resource billing parameters resolved by the engine at create time

autoscaleThreshold.description: Effective autoscale thresholds (provider profile merged with any explicit config)

scaleInCpuPercent.description: CPU % below which a scale-in event fires

scaleOutCpuPercent.description: CPU % that triggers a scale-out event

behaviorModel.description: Latency simulation model and GPU interconnect topology parameters for this resource. latencyPath identifies which engine path runs at step time. Two distinct model components: (1) throughput scaling — topologyThroughputFactor (resolveTopologyScalingFactor) bounds effective token capacity; topologyThroughputCalibrationStatus and topologyIsLegacyBaseline qualify that factor. (2) latency shape — topologyTtftFactor + topologyDecodeFactor (resolveTopologyLatencyFactors) scale TTFT and decode curves; topologyCalibrationStatus qualifies those factors. Both components are present on inferenceMode Kubernetes clusters; latencyPath is present on all resource types.

acceleratorResolution.description: 'catalog' = accelerator matched ACCELERATOR_TOKENS_PER_SEC; 'fallback' = unrecognised, defaults substituted (TTFT 600 ms, decode 700 tok/s, perNodeTokens 500)

behaviourFidelity.description: 'modeled' = parameters from the performance catalog; 'estimated' = defaults substituted

description.description: Human-readable description of the latency model applied to this resource

latencyPath.description: Canonical latency simulation path identifier, e.g. 'gpu-inference/ttft-decode' or 'generic-kubernetes/load-saturation'. Machine-match against LATENCY_PATHS constants — do not string-parse.

modelingNote.description: Provenance disclaimer for latency figures. On inferenceMode clusters states that TTFT/P95/P99 are CWM simulation-model estimates from accelerator catalog parameters, not externally measured benchmarks. When topology is omitted also notes the legacy-baseline assumption (topologyThroughputFactor=1.0).

topologyCalibrationStatus.description: Calibration status of the TTFT+decode latency factors (resolveTopologyLatencyFactors). Entirely separate from topologyThroughputCalibrationStatus, which covers throughput scaling.

topologyDecodeFactor.description: Decode-rate latency scaling factor applied by the engine's GPU inference model (resolveTopologyLatencyFactors). Describes the TTFT+decode latency dimension — distinct from the throughput scaling factor.

topologyInterNode.description: Raw characteristics.topology.interNode value or null when absent

topologyIntraNode.description: Raw characteristics.topology.intraNode value ('pcie', 'nvlink', 'nvlink-nvswitch', 'infiniband') or null when absent

topologyIsLegacyBaseline.description: true when topology.intraNode was absent or unrecognised, meaning topologyThroughputFactor=1.0 reflects the pre-topology legacy baseline (not a fabric-specific measurement). false when an explicit, recognised intraNode value was supplied and the throughput factor is topology-modelled.

topologyNodeCount.description: Node count used when resolving topology latency factors (≥ 1)

topologyThroughputCalibrationStatus.description: Calibration status of the throughput scaling factor (resolveTopologyScalingFactor). Distinct from topologyCalibrationStatus, which covers TTFT+decode latency factors. 'estimated' for all current intraNode coefficients (engineering assumptions from bandwidth arithmetic). 'not_applicable' on non-inferenceMode resources. Reserve 'calibrated' for when a directly measured per-request throughput ratio is added.

topologyThroughputFactor.description: Throughput scaling coefficient applied by resolveTopologyScalingFactor to this cluster's token capacity (nodes × perNodeTokensPerSec × factor × gpuUtil/100). 1.0 when topology.intraNode is absent or unrecognised (legacy baseline, topologyIsLegacyBaseline=true). Known fabric penalties: pcie≈0.70, nvlink≈0.85, nvlink-nvswitch≈0.92, infiniband≈1.0. Entirely separate from topologyTtftFactor/topologyDecodeFactor, which describe the TTFT+decode latency model.

topologyTtftFactor.description: TTFT latency scaling factor applied by the engine's GPU inference model (resolveTopologyLatencyFactors). Describes the TTFT+decode latency dimension — distinct from the throughput scaling factor.

billingFloorCostPerHour.description: Minimum cluster cost in USD/hr (cost at billingFloorNodes)

billingFloorNodes.description: Minimum node count the engine will ever bill — scale-in cannot go below this

capacityExplanation.description: Declared or estimated GKE capacity, independent of pricing coverage; unresolved is not zero capacity.

capacityProvenance.description: Source of effective capacity: explicit caller field, provider catalog, generic fallback, or cpu_model_estimate (EKS worker CPU-curve assumption, not measured/calibrated capacity)

connectionLimitProvenance.description: Admission budget origin, not an observed server parameter or application pool size. Tier heuristics are assumptions, not provider max_connections evidence.

controlPlaneFeePerHour.description: Cost-only cluster management fee in USD/hr; it does not represent control-plane CPU, throttling, or recovery telemetry

currentNodesCostPerHour.description: Total cluster cost at the current node count (control plane + nodes × rate) × spotFactor in USD/hr

effectiveCpuCapacityRps.description: CPU-curve denominator after applying the provider threshold to explicit capacityRps

nodePools.description: Per-pool billing details for multi-pool clusters (absent on single-pool clusters)

perNodeRatePerHour.description: Per-node billing rate in USD/hr. Omitted when unavailable; never zero as a substitute. Incomplete GKE totals are known-components subtotals, not complete cluster prices.

perNodeTokensPerSec.description: Modelled per-node token throughput at full utilisation (tokens/sec) — present only on inference-mode kubernetes resources

rateProvenance.description: Trust metadata for the resolved rate: pricing basis (on-demand/spot/estimated/list), lookup path, and the date the constant was last verified against the provider's public pricing page. Present on compute, database, and GPU inference resources; absent on resource types where no rate is resolved.

architecture.description: Fargate task architecture when architecture-specific billing applies

basis.description: Pricing basis: on-demand, spot, a flat estimate, or published list pricing

components.description: Every GKE worker and included management-fee component, with selected evidence; dates stay null when not recorded.

lastVerified.description: ISO-8601 date the constant was last cross-checked against the provider's pricing page; null when unknown

region.description: Region the verified rate applies to; null for region-uniform pricing

resolution.description: Which lookup path resolved the rate

sku.description: Exact catalog SKU used for this rate, when available

source.description: Official pricing source URL, when verified

requestServing.description: Resolved request-serving settings. For Fargate, aggregateCapacityRps is desiredTaskCount × this service's own rate, maxAggregateCapacityRps uses maxTaskCount, and perTaskCapacityEvidence distinguishes assumptions from caller-asserted documentation/measurement or provider catalog data.

resolvedConnectionLimit.description: Effective max-connection limit the engine uses for connection-pressure modelling (database resources)

resolvedCostMultiplier.description: Effective cost multiplier the engine applies to the base provider rate for this resource

resolvedGpuRatePerNode.description: Resolved GPU node billing rate in USD/hr — present only on inference-mode kubernetes resources

resolvedHourlyRate.description: Resolved hourly billing rate in USD/hr (base rate × multiplier)

resolvedMaxThroughputRps.description: Per-node RPS ceiling the engine uses for load and autoscale calculations

resolvedSkuLabel.description: The GPU SKU that was matched (e.g. 'a100-80gb') or a fallback label naming the provider default — present only on inference-mode kubernetes resources

resolvedStorageTier.description: Storage tier / size string used to resolve pricing (database resources)

spotFactor.description: Spot-instance discount factor applied to the node cost (absent = 1, i.e. no discount)

workerPriceEvidence.description: Matched worker source identity, units, components, hardware and bundled SSD inclusion; absent for unverified quotes.

offeredRps.description: Aggregate offered requests per second represented by metrics.offeredRps provenance

predictionEffectiveConfigHash.description: Versioned prediction hash over replay startup inputs, engine version, and calibration identity.

pricedResourceSubtotalPerHour.description: Priced-resource subtotal in USD/hr when costStatus is incomplete; not the full cluster cost.

reason.description: fairness_yield means a committed prefix released admission for queued simulations. Continue remaining steps with a new operationId and the returned checkpoint; replaying the same operation returns its original outcome.

effectiveConfigHash.description: Original replay-only SHA-256 of the effective six-control startup configuration; top-level effectiveConfigHash is the versioned prediction identity.

scenarioHash.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the persisted scenario graph and attached traffic-pattern order

aggregateCapacityRps.description: Capacity includes active tasks, including tasks draining during scale-down.

drainingTasks.description: Excess running Fargate tasks still serving and billing during scale-down.

residualCostDefinition.description: Definition of residual cost; total cost remains the complete billed total.

residualCostPerHour.description: Subtotal of unavailable, parked, or stopped resource costs; healthy/degraded idle resources, including ALBs, are excluded.

resilienceDiagnostics.description: Bounded resilience diagnostics summary (compact mode). Absent when the resilience model did not run. Use simulation.compare_resilience for full per-path detail.

bounded.description: True when a generated-traffic, traversal-work, or cascade-depth bound truncated model work

capacityByResource.description: Unique logical dependency resources; each appears once even when several paths reference it. When values are finite, nominalCapacityRps minus warmupCapacityLossRps (members still warming) and healthCapacityLossRps (unavailable or degraded members) equals routableCapacityRps, within rounding.

healthCapacityLossRps.description: Aggregate capacity lost because members are unavailable or degraded; zero means no modeled member-health loss

nominalCapacityRps.description: Aggregate capacity before warm-up and member-health reductions; null means no finite capacity ceiling is known

resourceId.description: Logical resource ID used by one or more resilience dependency paths

role.description: Whether this resource is a dependency source, target, or both

routableCapacityRps.description: Aggregate capacity available to this logical resource after modeled warm-up and member health; null means no finite capacity ceiling is known

warmupCapacityLossRps.description: Aggregate capacity lost because fleet members are still warming up; zero means no modeled warm-up loss

incidentOutcome.description: Incident outcome: stable | degraded | cascading | protected | recovered

pathCount.description: Number of dependency paths evaluated this step

modelScope.const: generic-pod-lifecycle; modeled estimates, not controller or proxy parity

availabilityState.description: Availability derived from lifecycle and routed traffic: available = serving normally, degraded = critical/warning but still serving, unavailable = failed/parked, scaled_to_zero and cold_start = Fargate no-task states

failureLifecycle.description: Read-only failure lifecycle marker when the backend identifies a quick injection or typed instance failure

isRoutable.description: Whether this compute/Kubernetes resource can receive traffic in this step; false distinguishes a failed/parked node from a critical node still serving

recoveryBlockedReason.description: Engine recovery guard currently preventing cooldown progress, when present (for example failure_park_window or idle_cpu_floor)

recoveryProgress.description: Read-only recovery progress; poll simulation.step until state is healthy, then use simulation.metrics to inspect the result

routedRps.description: Requests per second routed to this resource this step (compute/kubernetes only)

routingState.description: Read-only current routing state for a resource with failure lifecycle telemetry

retryAmplificationFactor.description: (Original offered RPS + generated retry RPS) / original offered RPS; an amplification measure, not capacity or goodput. Values > 1.0 = amplification risk. null = model ran but no traffic. Absent = resilience model disabled.

scenarioHash.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the persisted scenario graph and attached traffic-pattern order

tokensPerSecond.description: Inference throughput in tokens/second — present only on GPU inference simulations

datasetGiB.description: Total resident-memory plateau in GiB, INCLUDING initialGiB; not additional allocation or on-disk dataset bytes. Must be >= initialGiB. Other services and host reserve are separate. Example: initialGiB=1, datasetGiB=4 grows from 1 to 4 GiB, not 5 GiB; a 100 GiB input file does not imply 100 GiB resident memory.

initialGiB.description: Starting total resident working-set memory in GiB for this batch container, not dataset file size.
